apps.name: Dispatcher
apps.description: Schedule outbound pickups and inbound arrivals, track load progress, and view daily timelines.
apps.releaseNotes:
Dispatcher 1.1.3

Swipe left or right on Inbounds and Outbounds to select the next or previous filter. A swipe must cover at least a quarter of the page width, with a 96 dp minimum, before switching on release. Short swipes, vertical scrolling, and search-field gestures do not switch filters. The Today page retains its existing timeline gestures.

Loading dots on Print and Start Loading buttons now draw as one compact indicator, preventing device fonts or display sizes from wrapping the dots onto another line.

Install over the existing app to retain saved settings and authorization. The package ID and signing certificate are unchanged.

apps.name: MES Radio
apps.description: Push-to-talk for your MES team. Talk on radio channels and replay received voice.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Radio 1.0.6

Broadcast now uses a compact speaker toggle while your normal channel stays selected. All channels shows the total online headcount. The yellow icon has no button background; users without permission see a gray speaker with a ban badge.
Broadcast mode adds a soft yellow inner edge glow and Hold to broadcast. While transmitting, the glow grows with microphone loudness and settles during pauses instead of pulsing on a timer. Reduced-motion settings keep a steady glow.
Broadcast speaker assignments and global priority remain enforced by the server.

Steadier participant avatars with approximate location: ignores location noise within the reported accuracy and limits sudden relative movement.
Phones travelling together no longer shift the radar relationship just because one phone's next fix arrives first. Real movement updates gradually; missing or stale locations remain unavailable.
Broadcast settings now show only All channels. Broadcast priority and assigned speaker permissions are unchanged.

Enable the Broadcast speaker to speak to every joined channel. Broadcast has highest priority and interrupts ordinary channel speech.
Listeners remain on their selected channel and receive Broadcast automatically. Ordinary Talk is unavailable during Broadcast; interrupted speakers must release and press again afterward.
Broadcast announcements retain the yellow history cards and speaker badges in the receiving channel's history.
Existing assigned Broadcast speaker permissions still apply.
Keeps the connection recovery improvements and Quiet, Medium and Loud listening levels from previous patches.

Android 9 or newer. Updates MES Radio in place and preserves sign-in, settings and voice history. Do not uninstall before updating.

Two-phone feedback and real-world unstable-network testing remain pending.

apps.name: MES Run Beta
apps.description: Run production, coordinate staff, and follow line progress using isolated sample data.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Run Beta 10 - Product Catalog Review

The beta now shows the full list of 23 available MES product names and identifying codes. Search by name or code and review the product selected on the production schedule. The catalog is supplied by the hosted beta service; this release marks the product-name review milestone.

Other data remains sample data pending review: staff, attendance, line layouts, targets, raw materials, machine parameters and packaging. Existing production history retains its saved names and values. MES Run focuses on production records; pallet label printing belongs to a separate app.

Update MES Run Beta in MES Store, then pull down to refresh. Try selecting a scheduled product and choosing another product from the full list. If an older saved setup still shows its original sample name, select the product again from the refreshed list. The sample supervisor PIN, package and signing identity are unchanged.

This release retains the existing UI and production workflow. The catalog update passed three backend integration checks and hosted verification of all 23 product identities, schedule quantity and preservation of existing records. The signed release build and 36 model tests passed; lint has zero errors and 17 existing warnings. The signing certificate and isolated sample endpoint were verified. Native UI and full API-driven Android lifecycle tests were not repeated for this version-only Android change.

Signed-release installation and installation through MES Store remain unverified because automatic approval review previously blocked those checks. The publisher verifies the downloadable APK checksum. Physical printing, inspector submissions and live Andon inputs are outside this release.

apps.name: MES Store
apps.description: Your MES apps and updates, together in one place.
apps.releaseNotes:
MES Store 1.2.16

MES Store now checks for updates when you return to it, every five minutes while it stays open, and when the connection comes back while the store is open. A one-minute cooldown prevents repeated checks during quick app switches.

Background update checks now run approximately hourly instead of daily, subject to Android battery and network scheduling. Existing daily schedules are upgraded automatically.

Catalog checks can use any internet connection. The unmetered-only setting continues to apply to automatic APK downloads. Automatic checks still respect your setting, and Android still asks before installing updates.

Install over MES Store to preserve settings and downloads. Android 9 or newer; the package ID and release signing key are unchanged.
